_note: Published numbers for the comparison tables. Values are deliberately null:
fill each one by reading it off the cited paper (or its official repo) and
flip 'verified' to true. icce/eval/tables.py refuses to typeset an
unverified row, so nothing unchecked can reach the submitted PDF.
Every method carries a 'tier'. Tables group by tier and label the groups,
because these are not one league:
supervised  trained on this dataset's own training split. A specialist
with in-domain labels; reported as a reference ceiling, not
zero-shot   no training on this dataset. Our actual peer group.

methods.name: TinyCD
methods._source: F1/IoU confirmed by two independent sources (arXiv:2207.13159 abstract and the emergentmind summary of it), both giving 91.05 / 83.57. Precision and recall are left null on purpose: the only value seen for them (92.68 / 89.47, skip-connection variant) came from a single secondary summary, and this file's rule is that nothing unchecked is typeset. Read them off the paper's table before submission.

methods.name: AnyChange (SAM zero-shot)
methods._source: arXiv:2402.01188 Table 'Zero-shot Object Change Proposals', ViT-B row (best automatic F1 of the three backbones; ViT-L 21.9, ViT-H 23.0). IoU is not reported by the paper. Full 128-tile LEVIR-CD test split.

methods.name: AnyChange-H + 3-point query
methods._source: arXiv:2402.01188 Table 'Zero-shot Object-centric Change Detection'. Human-in-the-loop: three point queries per image. Listed so the comparison is not read as cherry-picking the weakest AnyChange setting.

levir_cc._protocol: LEVIR-CC test split, 5 references per pair, coco-caption metrics

_note: Caption files produced by running a published model's released checkpoint
on the LEVIR-CC test split. Scoring these with Change-Fact-Score is what
gives our factuality metric an external reference point -- without it a
reviewer can fairly say we invented a metric and only measured ourselves.
Format: JSON or JSONL of {pair_id: caption} or {'key','text'} records.
